content: I'll start by reading the test image to analyze its visual features.

The test image shows two banana fruits — the top one has irregular dark black/brown spots and patches on the yellow skin, and the bottom one shows severe dark/black lesions covering much of the fruit surface. This is clearly a fruit disease, not a leaf disease. The pattern of spreading dark spots is most consistent with Anthracnose.

**Analysis of the test image:**
- Affected part: **banana fruit** (not leaves)
- Top banana: yellow background with irregular dark black/brown spots and patches scattered across the surface
- Bottom banana: severe advancement with large coalescing black lesions covering most of the fruit
- The spots are irregular, dark, and spreading — classic post-harvest fruit infection pattern

**Ruling out other classes:**
- Bunchy_Top, Cordana_Leaf_Spot, Panama_Disease, Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka — all affect **leaves**, not fruit
- Cigar_End_Rot — affects the **tip/end** of the banana, not widespread spots across the fruit surface
- **Anthracnose** — caused by *Colletotrichum musae*, produces exactly this pattern: dark irregular black/brown spots on banana fruit skin that coalesce and spread, matching both bananas shown
